subject.title: feat(plugins): expose requester context to tool hooks

question: Should `ctx.requester` be a permanent public plugin authorization contract whose value is defined per incoming turn, including steered messages in an existing run?
rationale: The immediate stale-context defect is repairable, but maintainers must confirm the long-term API guarantee for requester provenance, freshness, and the supported steering semantics before exposing it as a stable authorization surface.

options.title: Sponsor per-turn requester semantics
options.body: Define requester as the authenticated sender of each input that can cause a tool call, then require the implementation and tests to refresh it across steering and native relays.

options.title: Keep the surface internal for now
options.body: Do not publish this plugin hook field until the full cross-turn requester-provenance contract has an approved owner and boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor per-turn requester semantics
recommendation.body: Define requester as the authenticated sender of each input that can cause a tool call, then require the implementation and tests to refresh it across steering and native relays.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored both the focused public API proposal and the earlier design exploration that frames the unresolved authorization boundary.
